## 4\. An explicit uniform entropy contraction

Choose

\[
q=\frac m{16},
\qquad
\boxed{
\delta=\frac{m}{32(1+f_+/f_-)}
=\frac m{16\Gamma}.
}
\]

Let \(H_0=H(c(0)|p)\), \(H_\tau=H(c(\tau)|p)\)\.

If \(H_\tau\leq H_0/2\), then certainly

\[
H_\tau\leq(1-\delta)H_0.
\]

Otherwise, put \(h=H_\tau/H_0>1/2\)\. Equations (3)–(4) imply

\[
\sqrt{mh}
\leq \sqrt2q+\sqrt{\Gamma(1-h)}.
\]

Since \(m\leq1\) and \(q=m/16\), rearranging yields

\[
1-h\geq\frac m{16\Gamma}=\delta.
\]

Thus, in both cases,

\[
\boxed{
H(c(\tau)|p)\leq(1-\delta)H(c(0)|p).
}
\tag{5}
\]

The contraction is uniform in \(N\), the initial spatial profile and the solution's future derivatives. The constants depend only on the supplied friction data and \(m\)\.

## 5\. Arbitrarily prescribed entropy decay

Choose the rational time

\[
\boxed{\tau=\frac{\delta}{2\chi}.}
\]

Use the accepted polynomial-resource scalar construction to produce one stationary rational-trigonometric divergence-free velocity \(b\) satisfying

\[
\boxed{
\|e^{\tau(\lambda\Delta-b\cdot\nabla)}P_0\|_{2\to2}
\leq\frac m{16}.
}
\tag{6}
\]

Applying (5) successively on intervals of length \(\tau\), and using entropy monotonicity between their endpoints, gives

\[
H(c(t)|p)
\leq (1-\delta)^{\lfloor t/\tau\rfloor}H(c_0|p).
\]

Because \(-\log(1-\delta)\geq\delta\),

\[
\boxed{
H(c(t)|\bar c)
\leq
\frac1{1-\delta}e^{-2\chi t}H(c_0|\bar c)
\leq
\frac1{1-\delta}e^{-\chi t}H(c_0|\bar c).
}
\tag{7}
\]

Therefore the entropy-decay prefactor can be chosen explicitly as

\[
\boxed{C=(1-\delta)^{-1}<2.}
\]

The velocity is computed from rational inputs \((\lambda,\tau,m/16)\)\. Its construction costs are consequently bounded by the accepted scalar primitive's explicit polynomial evaluated on those rational quantities. No new PDE or numerical oracle is required.

**Precisely established scope\:** Equation (7) holds for every global Maxwell–Stefan solution satisfying the simplex constraint, flux relations, and entropy-dissipation inequality, with sufficient weak regularity for the comparison argument. It also holds on every interval of existence of a classical solution.

This proves the requested arbitrary-rate entropy estimate *conditional on global entropy-admissible solvability*\. It does not yet prove global strong solvability.

## 7\. A class for which the full strong theorem is established

The construction does prove the entire requested result for **arbitrary \(N\) when all frictions are equal**\.

Suppose \(f_{ij}=f>0\) for every pair. Using the flux constraint,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\nabla c_i
&=f\sum_{j\ne i}(c_iJ_j-c_jJ_i)\\
&=-fJ_i.
\end{aligned}
\]

Consequently,

\[
\boxed{
\partial_t c_i+b\cdot\nabla c_i
=\frac1f\Delta c_i
\qquad(i=1,\ldots,N).
}
\]

These are independent scalar advection–diffusion equations.

The scalar maximum principle preserves the simplex, parabolic regularity gives unique global classical solutions, and the strictly positive heat kernel gives \(c_i(t,x)>0\) for every \(t>0\) whenever \(\bar c_i\geq m\)\.

Equation (7) supplies the prescribed exponential entropy decay using the same field and the same computable bounds.

This includes every two-species Maxwell–Stefan system.
